items.title: Craving and Hatred, and the Elephant Who Learned Cruelty From Its Neighbours

items.zh: 貪者，謂由親近不善丈夫、聞非正法、不如理作意故，及由任運失念故，於外及內可愛境界，若分別、不分別染著為體。
items.en: As for craving: it arises through keeping bad company, hearing false teachings, unsound attention, or a spontaneous lapse of mindfulness, and consists, whether deliberately reasoned or spontaneous, in a defiled attachment towards agreeable objects, whether external or internal to oneself.

items.zh: 恚者，謂由親近不善丈夫、聞非正法、不如理作意故，及由任運失念故，於外及內非愛境界，若分別、不分別憎恚為體。
items.en: As for hatred: it arises through keeping bad company, hearing false teachings, unsound attention, or a spontaneous lapse of mindfulness, and consists, whether deliberately reasoned or spontaneous, in a resentful aversion towards disagreeable objects, whether external or internal to oneself.

items.title: Conceit, Ignorance, and Doubt Complete the Ten Fundamental Afflictions

items.zh: 慢者，謂由親近不善丈夫、聞非正法、不如理作意故，及由任運失念故，於外及內高下勝劣，若分別、不分別高舉為體。
items.en: As for conceit: it arises through keeping bad company, hearing false teachings, unsound attention, or a spontaneous lapse of mindfulness, and consists, whether deliberately reasoned or spontaneous, in an inflated self-regard concerning relative superiority or inferiority, in age or in virtue, whether towards oneself or towards others.

items.zh: 無明者，謂由親近不善丈夫、聞非正法、不如理作意故，及由任運失念故，於所知事，若分別、不分別染污無知為體。疑者，謂由親近不善丈夫、聞非正法、不如理作意故，即於所知事，唯用分別異覺為體。
items.en: As for ignorance: it arises through keeping bad company, hearing false teachings, unsound attention, or a spontaneous lapse of mindfulness, and consists, whether deliberately reasoned or spontaneous, in a defiled unknowing regarding what should be known. As for doubt: it arises through keeping bad company, hearing false teachings, and unsound attention, and consists, always through deliberate reasoning, in a wavering, contrary understanding regarding what should be known.

items.title: Six Causes Behind Every Affliction — a Practical Map for Where They Actually Come From

items.zh: 煩惱因者，謂六種因。一、由所依故，二、由所緣故，三、由親近故，四、由邪教故，五、由數習故，六、由作意故。由此六因，起諸煩惱。
items.en: As for the causes of affliction: there are six kinds of cause. First, through its basis; second, through its object; third, through association; fourth, through false teaching; fifth, through habituation; sixth, through attention. It is through these six causes that every affliction arises.

items.zh: 所依故者，謂由隨眠起諸煩惱。所緣故者，謂順煩惱境界現前。親近故者，謂由隨學不善丈夫。邪教故者，謂由聞非正法。數習故者，謂由先殖數習力勢。作意故者，謂由發起不如理作意故，諸煩惱生。
items.en: Through its basis: affliction arises from its own latent seed. Through its object: an object capable of provoking affliction actually presents itself. Through association: one follows and learns from an unwholesome person. Through false teaching: one hears a teaching that is not the true Dharma. Through habituation: the accumulated force of past repetition has already been planted. Through attention: unsound reasoning attention is what actually gives rise to every affliction.

items.title: Seven Stages of Affliction, From Dormant Seed to Full Intensity

items.zh: 煩惱位者：略有七種。一、隨眠位，二、纏位，三、分別起位，四、俱生位，五、耎位，六、中位，七、上位。
items.en: As for the stages of affliction: there are, briefly, seven. First, the stage of the latent seed; second, the stage of active manifestation; third, the stage of deliberately-reasoned arising; fourth, the stage of innate arising; fifth, the mild stage; sixth, the middling stage; seventh, the intense stage.

items.zh: 由二緣故，煩惱隨眠之所隨眠。一、由種子隨逐故；二、由彼增上事故。
items.en: It is through two conditions that affliction's latent tendency lies latent: first, because its seed continues to trail along uninterrupted; second, because whenever affliction actively manifests, it further reinforces and strengthens that same seed.

items.title: Two Gateways of Affliction: How the Manifest Form Actually Harms

items.zh: 煩惱門者，略由二門煩惱所惱。謂由纏門及隨眠門。纏門有五種。一、由不寂靜住故；二、由障礙善故；三、由發起惡趣惡行故；四、由攝受現法鄙賤故；五、由能感生等苦故。
items.en: As for affliction's gateways: briefly, a being is troubled by affliction through two gateways — the gateway of active manifestation and the gateway of the latent seed. The gateway of active manifestation has five aspects: first, it disturbs one's abiding peace; second, it obstructs what is wholesome; third, it gives rise to unwholesome conduct leading to an unfortunate destiny; fourth, it draws present contempt upon oneself; fifth, it brings about the suffering of rebirth and the rest.

items.zh: 云何隨眠門所惱？謂與諸纏作所依故，及能引發生等苦故。
items.en: How is a being troubled through the gateway of the latent seed? Because it serves as the basis for every active manifestation, and because it too brings about the suffering of rebirth and the rest.

items.title: Seven Further Gateways That Specifically Block the Path of Seeing and Cultivation

items.zh: 又由七門，一切煩惱於見及修能為障礙應知。謂邪解了故，不解了故，解了不解了故，邪解了迷執故，彼因依處故，彼怖所生故，任運現行故。
items.en: Further, it should be understood that every affliction obstructs the path of seeing and the path of cultivation through seven gateways: through mistaken understanding; through simple non-understanding; through a half-formed understanding that both understands and fails to; through mistaken understanding compounded by clinging; through serving as the mutual basis of suffering and its origin; through the fear arising from cessation and the path; and through spontaneous, innate manifestation.

items.title: Six Marks of the Most Intense Grade of Affliction

items.zh: 云何煩惱上品相？謂猛利相及尤重相。此相略有六種。一、由犯故；二、由生故；三、由相續故；四、由事故；五、由起惡業故；六、由究竟故。由犯故者，謂由此煩惱纏故，毀犯一切所有學處。由生故者，謂由此故，生於欲界苦惡趣中。由相續故者，謂貪等行、諸根成熟少年盛壯、無涅槃法者。
items.en: What is the mark of affliction at its most intense grade? It is the mark of being fierce and the mark of being especially weighty. This mark, briefly, has six aspects. First, through transgression: by reason of this affliction manifesting, one violates every precept one holds. Second, through the rebirth it produces: by reason of this affliction, one is reborn into the desire realm's suffering-filled unfortunate destinies. Third, through its continuity: it is found in those whose conduct is dominated by craving and the like, whose faculties have reached the full vigour of youth or prime adulthood, and who lack any seed of awakening at all.

items.zh: 由事故者，謂緣尊重田，若緣功德田，若緣不應行田而起。由起惡業故者，謂由此煩惱纏故，以增上適悅心起身語業。由究竟故者，謂此自性上品所攝，最初耎對治道之所斷故。
items.en: Fourth, through its object: it arises directed at a field deserving reverence, a field of genuine merit, or a field that should never be treated this way at all. Fifth, through generating unwholesome action: by reason of this affliction manifesting, one performs bodily and verbal deeds with a heightened sense of pleasure and satisfaction. Sixth, through its ultimate removal: this affliction, belonging by its very nature to the superior grade, is nonetheless the very first to be severed even by the mildest degree of the antidote path.

items.title: Seven Distortions: Mistaking Permanence, Pleasure, Purity, and Self Where None Exist

items.zh: 煩惱顛倒攝者，謂七顛倒。一、想倒，二、見倒，三、心倒，四、於無常常倒，五、於苦樂倒，六、於不淨淨倒，七、於無我我倒。
items.en: As for what affliction is subsumed under distortion: it refers to seven distortions. First, distortion of perception; second, distortion of view; third, distortion of mind; fourth, distortion regarding the impermanent as permanent; fifth, distortion regarding suffering as pleasure; sixth, distortion regarding the impure as pure; seventh, distortion regarding what is without self as having a self.

items.zh: 想倒者，謂於無常、苦、不淨、無我中，起常、樂、淨、我妄想分別。見倒者，謂即於彼妄想所分別中，忍可欲樂，建立執著。心倒者，謂即於彼所執著中貪等煩惱。
items.en: Distortion of perception is the mistaken conceptual grasp, applied to what is actually impermanent, suffering, impure, and without self, of permanence, pleasure, purity, and self. Distortion of view is the further step of endorsing and delighting in that very mistaken conceptual grasp, and establishing and clinging to it as a position. Distortion of mind is the craving and other affliction that arises within what has thereby been clung to.

items.title: Root, Substance, and Outflow: How the Ten Fundamental Afflictions Map Onto Distortion

items.zh: 當知煩惱略有三種。或有煩惱是倒根本，或有煩惱是顛倒體，或有煩惱是倒等流。倒根本者，謂無明。顛倒體者，謂薩迦耶見、邊執見一分、見取、戒禁取，及貪。倒等流者，謂邪見、邊執見一分、恚、慢及疑。
items.en: It should be understood that affliction, briefly, falls into three kinds: some affliction is the root of distortion, some is the very substance of distortion, and some is distortion's own outflow. The root of distortion is ignorance. The substance of distortion is self-view, one portion of extreme views, view-grasping, precept-grasping, and craving. Distortion's outflow is wrong view, the remaining portion of extreme views, hatred, conceit, and doubt.

items.zh: 此中薩迦耶見是無我我倒，邊執見一分是無常常倒，見取是不淨淨倒，戒禁取是於苦樂倒。貪通二種，謂不淨淨倒及於苦樂倒。
items.en: Here, self-view is the distortion of self in the non-self; one portion of extreme views is the distortion of permanence in the impermanent; view-grasping is the distortion of purity in the impure; precept-grasping is the distortion of pleasure in suffering. Craving runs through both the distortion of purity in the impure and the distortion of pleasure in suffering.

blocks.text: Today's reading is the most directly useful in the fascicle for daily practice. After the five dull afflictions, the treatise gives six causes of affliction, seven stages from dormant seed to full intensity, and seven distortions. Each list is a tool for watching the mind.

**Craving** (貪) is "defiled attachment towards agreeable objects, external or internal". **Hatred** (恚) is its opposite towards disagreeable ones. Master Cháng Bǎi's story about the power of surroundings: a king's elephant was kept near a monastery, where it heard monks chant and practise mindfulness every day, and it grew gentle; moved near a slaughterhouse, it grew fierce.

**Conceit** (慢) measures oneself against others "in age, superior and inferior". **Ignorance** (無明) is not knowing what should be known. Venerable Miào Jìng tells why Cūḍapanthaka was so dull in his last life: once a learned master of the canon, he had been stingy with the Dharma. **Doubt** (疑) is indecision about the truths.

items: **Basis**: the latent seed. Master Cháng Bǎi: a sage "passes through a hundred flowers with not a leaf clinging", because he has no such seeds.
**Habituation**. Venerable Miào Jìng: "like a little bird learning to fly, beating its wings again and again".

blocks.text: Both teachers single out the last. Master Cháng Bǎi: "Facing the same object, some become afflicted and some don't; whether attention is sound is the key." Venerable Miào Jìng compares attention to the gatekeeper of a monastery, who decides who comes in. (Compare Day 2 and Day 17.)

Affliction exists as a latent seed, then as active manifestation; arises deliberately (from false teaching) or innately; and is mild, middling, or intense. A latent seed persists by "trailing along" in the ālayavijñāna and by being reinforced. Venerable Miào Jìng: deprived of reinforcement, "the seed's power weakens, and it withers". This is why restraint works even before insight: what is not fed grows weaker.

Affliction troubles beings through two gateways: manifestation (it disturbs the mind now, leads to wrongdoing, and draws present contempt, even legal punishment) and the latent seed. Venerable Miào Jìng: the seed is "actually the most formidable", because it brings birth, ageing, sickness, and death.

subs.head: Six marks of the intense grade

blocks.text: Intense affliction is "fierce" (hard to subdue once active) and "weighty" (flaring up hugely over small matters), and is directed at the wrong objects: parents, the Three Jewels, or the poor. Then a surprising mark: the intense grade is cut *first*, by the mildest antidote. Master Cháng Bǎi: coarse afflictions are easy to see; subtle ones hide and need the strongest wisdom.

Distortions of perception, view, and mind, and the four of Day 3: permanence, pleasure, purity, and self where there are none. Master Cháng Bǎi: perception is the root distortion; view distortion belongs mostly to thinkers, mind distortion to everyone.

**Ignorance is the root** of distortion. Venerable Miào Jìng: "Ignorance's most powerful effect is clinging to everything as real"; we glimpse this only "on waking from a dream", when the sense of reality wavers for a moment.

quiz.q: Master Cháng Bǎi tells of an elephant to show the effect of bad company. What happens?
options: the elephant, kept near a monastery, heard monks practising mindfulness and chanting daily; moved near a slaughterhouse, it grew fierce with anger
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The trainer kept the elephant near a monastery, where monks practised the four foundations of mindfulness and chanted every day"; later "it was moved to live near a pig slaughterhouse"; "this shows that keeping bad company, over time, breeds great anger — and likewise other afflictions."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the six causes of affliction?
options: basis, object, association, false teaching, habituation, attention
quiz.why: "First, through its basis; second, through its object; third, through association; fourth, through false teaching; fifth, through habituation; sixth, through attention." Basis is the latent seed; object, a provoking object present; association, following bad people; false teaching, hearing non-Dharma; habituation, past repetition; attention, unsound attention.

quiz.q: Of the six causes, which do both teachers stress as the key?
options: attention — facing the same object, some get afflicted and some don't; sound attention is the key; Venerable Miào Jìng likens it to the gatekeeper of a monastery school
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Facing the same object, some become afflicted and some don't — whether attention is sound is the key." Venerable Miào Jìng: "The gatekeeper can be likened to attention — not the person outside." The object is whoever comes; attention decides whether to let them in.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the seven stages of affliction?
options: latent seed, active manifestation, conceptual arising, innate arising, mild, middling, intense
quiz.why: "First, the stage of the latent seed; second, the stage of active manifestation; third, … deliberately-reasoned arising; fourth, … innate arising; fifth, the mild stage; sixth, the middling stage; seventh, the intense stage." Venerable Miào Jìng: the last five "are all manifest wrappings."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, through which two gateways does affliction trouble beings?
options: the gateway of manifestation and that of the latent seed
quiz.why: "A being is troubled by affliction through two gateways — the gateway of active manifestation and the gateway of the latent seed." Master Cháng Bǎi: "the manifest gateway and the seed gateway." Manifestation has five aspects: disturbing peace, obstructing good, producing bad conduct, drawing present contempt, and bringing rebirth's suffering.

quiz.q: The sixth mark: the intense grade is severed first, by the mildest antidote. How do the teachers explain this?
options: surprisingly: coarse intense afflictions are easy to spot and fall to mild antidotes; subtle mild ones are hidden and need the strongest
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "This surprises us — we'd think the stronger the affliction, the higher the path needed." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Mild afflictions, being subtle, hard to notice, and hidden, require the strongest antidote to cut."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which affliction is "the root of distortion"?
quiz.why: "The root of distortion is ignorance. The substance of distortion is self-view, one portion of extreme views, view-grasping, precept-grasping, and craving. Distortion's outflow is wrong view, the remaining portion of extreme views, hatred, conceit, and doubt." Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Pixunji*: the "portion" in the substance is eternalism; annihilationism is outflow.
